solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Fielder, not long a member

parts.note: something not long is short
a leg is a limb, one of the body's members

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cricketer who has only recently joined the club.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORT LEG is a cricket fielding position close to the batter on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Short leg is a named close catching position in cricket, so the player standing there is a fielder.

clue.text: Hero of poem, Will's second, Hathaway, mostly, edited

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged
the second letter of the word Will is wanted
mostly means all but the last letter

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife Anne Hathaway, and Will himself, appear in a piece about a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: I from Will plus HATHAWA rearranged gives the answer. Longfellow's poem tells of this Ojibwe hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's narrative poem The Song of Hiawatha has him as its central figure.

clue.text: Misleading clue embarrassed husband getting it wrong

parts.note: an embarrassed face goes red
erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: An embarrassed husband makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a distraction that leads people off the true trail.

clue.text: Actual misprint

definitions.meaning: exact, taking words in their plain sense
a printer's term for a typing error

explanation.definitionFit: Literal means factual or word-for-word; in printing it also names a typo.

clue.text: First sign of grey parrot and crow?

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A grey parrot is compared with a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' is a bird in the surface, but here is the verb meaning exult.
explanation.definitionFit: To glory in something is to exult or crow over it.

clue.text: Race official from course

definitions.meaning: the person who signals the start of a race
the first course of a meal

explanation.definitionFit: A starter fires the gun to begin a race, and is also an appetiser.

clue.text: In favour of training, right? Right

parts.note: pro means for
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being in favour of exercise is correct, then confirms it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or appropriate.

clue.text: Inn, shortly to be refurbished, accommodating European

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something inside
refurbished means done up afresh, signalling rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A pub soon to be renovated takes in a European guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be refurbished' makes HOSTLRY from SHORTLY; 'accommodating' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned word for an inn or pub.

clue.text: Womaniser reluctant to visit a Brazilian port

parts.note: loth is an old spelling of loath, meaning unwilling
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport

explanation.surface: A philanderer is unwilling to travel to a South American harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, the seducer in a Rowe play, became a byword for a man who chases women.

clue.text: Criminal slot machine?

definitions.meaning: a one-armed gambling machine is nicknamed after a robber

explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber, and a fruit machine is a one-armed one, taking players' money.

clue.text: Appalling mutterer? Pa must get a hearing aid!

indicators.note: an appalling mess of letters signals that the words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child complains that dad, who mumbles dreadfully, needs something to help him hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appalling' rearranges MUTTERER and PA; 'must get' just links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The old horn-shaped device held to the ear was an early aid for the hard of hearing.

clue.text: Seemingly endless English learnt abroad

indicators.note: abroad in its sense of astray or all over the place signals rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A language learnt overseas feels as though it will never end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' reads as overseas in the surface, but here means scattered, rearranging the letters of learnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts forever, or appears to, hence endless in effect.

clue.text: Colonel knocked over a litre in one's pub

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A colonel spills a litre of drink in his own pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Your local is the pub nearest your home that you habitually visit.

clue.text: New trees planted in centre of Auckland will attract bird of prey

indicators.note: being planted in something means being set inside it
the centre of an eight-letter word is its middle pair of letters
new trees are made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fresh planting in the middle of a New Zealand city will draw a hunting bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges trees; 'planted in' sets the result inside the middle pair of Auckland, its central letters K and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers before swooping on prey.

clue.text: In woodwork, finally gets to carve a ship

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: to etch is to cut a design into a surface

explanation.surface: In woodwork class, someone at last gets to carve a model ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: I knew match ground — this one?

definitions.text: I knew match ground — this one?

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recognises which stadium a game was played at.
explanation.walkthrough: TWICKENHAM is the national rugby stadium in south-west London; 'ground' is the anagram signal and also points to the stadium in the whole-clue reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Twickenham is a famous sports ground, home of English rugby union.

clue.text: No mixer, one from our capital fellow ignored

indicators.note: the fellow is left out of the longer word

parts.note: for a British paper, someone from the capital is a Londoner
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A Londoner who is unsociable is snubbed by a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no mixer keeps to themselves, a solitary person.

clue.text: Boy girl bowled over

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Lisa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boy knocks over a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' looks like one phrase meaning astonished; split it, B for bowled and 'over' turning the girl backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a common masculine first name, so it fits the definition by example of a boy.

clue.text: Usher in dark bar

parts.note: black means dark
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: An usher stands in a gloomy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACK ROD is the official usher of the House of Lords in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Rod's full title is Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod.

clue.text: Quick and inclined to bite?

definitions.meaning: read literally, ... describes a creature given to nipping

explanation.definitionFit: Nippy is informal British for speedy, and literally describes something that nips.

clue.text: Pauper at first feels bitter about handouts

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter

parts.note: to resent is to feel bitter about

explanation.surface: A poor person resents receiving charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents are gifts, things handed out.

clue.text: Go with suit and tie

definitions.meaning: to complement or pair well with
to be a good fit for
a game or contest, as in a cup tie

explanation.definitionFit: Match means pair with, be fitting for, and a sporting contest or fixture.

clue.text: Short skirt? Mother points to bottom!

parts.note: a mini is a miniskirt
mum is mother

explanation.surface: A mother's short skirt draws attention to her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' looks like a backside but means the lowest level.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the lowest point, the very bottom of a range.

clue.text: One who harasses a runner

definitions.meaning: a person who harries or pesters

explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is one who harries, and also a cross-country runner.

clue.text: Girl could give a grown-up trouble

parts.note: a grown-up child is big
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A girl might cause problems for an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a girl's name, also an old word for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Fuel left out burst into flames

indicators.note: out means removed from the word

parts.note: lignite is brown coal, a fuel

explanation.surface: Fuel abandoned outside caught fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to catch fire.

clue.text: Cope with French general in coach

parts.note: to hack it is to cope
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A French general travels in a carriage, managing as best he can.
explanation.walkthrough: A HACKNEY carriage is a horse-drawn vehicle for hire; London taxis are still licensed as hackney carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is a hired horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: Rope male into group

indicators.note: into here means going inside, so the male pronoun is put within the word for a group

parts.note: a set is a group
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man is roped into joining a group.
explanation.walkthrough: On a sailing boat a sheet is a rope controlling a sail, not bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a nautical rope.

clue.text: Bird, with end of beak, snapped his finger

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
something snapped is broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird's beak tip catches a man's finger and breaks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' rearranges HISFINGER to INGFISHER, after K from 'end of beak'.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a brightly coloured diving bird.

clue.text: Receiving attention at home, manual worker

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer is being looked after at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in hand is being dealt with at present.

clue.text: Shed, old ramshackle hut by river

indicators.note: ramshackle means tumbledown, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A tumbledown hut stands beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small outbuilding such as a shed.

clue.text: Nutty, it is a rum dessert

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A pudding laced with rum is described as nutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.
